personas.description: You design or manage points and tier programs for a retailer, airline, hotel, or similar business.

personas.label: Salesforce consultants and admins

examDifficulty.heading: How challenging is the Loyalty Management AP exam?
examDifficulty.summary: This is a moderate exam about earning and redeeming points, tier changes, and the processes that apply loyalty rules.
bullets: 50 scored questions in 75 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
69% to pass, which is 35 correct answers out of 50.
Program design. Review point currencies, tiers, benefits, promotions, and vouchers.
Rules and transactions. Learn how transaction journals and program processes award or redeem points.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Create a small program in a trial org with two tiers and one promotion, then post sample transactions. Aim for at least 80% on practice questions before booking.

examFormat.heading: Loyalty Management AP exam format
examFormat.intro: Accredited Professional exams are delivered online. Questions commonly describe a loyalty program requirement:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: A scenario may ask how to give double points on a weekend or renew a member’s Gold status. Select the program setting or process that implements the rule.
bestWayToPass: Separate the currencies: Qualifying points affect tier status; non-qualifying points can be redeemed for rewards.
Follow the transaction: Purchases and activities are posted as journals that program processes evaluate.
Study program processes: Understand how rules govern accrual, redemption, and tier changes.
Practise promotions: Review bonus points, eligibility, date ranges, and member limits.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers Salesforce Loyalty Management program design and operations, including currencies, tiers, benefits, promotions, transaction journals, program processes, and point redemption. It has 60 questions in 90 minutes; confirm the current passing score in the official guide.

keyConcepts.h2: Loyalty Management AP: concepts to review

blocks.heading: Program structure, tiers, and points
blocks.body: A loyalty program contains its currencies, tiers, benefits, and rules. Qualifying points count toward a member’s tier status; non-qualifying points can be spent but do not affect status. Tier groups organize levels such as Silver, Gold, and Platinum. Each tier can have thresholds and benefits, such as free delivery or lounge access. Scheduled tier reviews determine whether a member advances, keeps their tier, or moves down.

blocks.heading: Accrual and redemption
blocks.body: A purchase, flight, or other activity is recorded as a transaction journal. Program processes evaluate journals and apply rules, such as awarding one point per dollar or a higher rate for Gold members. A redemption journal can trigger a process that subtracts points. Points can expire after a defined period, and the member ledger records balance changes so each earning, redemption, or expiry can be explained.

blocks.heading: Promotions and member engagement
blocks.body: Promotions encourage behavior such as earning double points on a weekend or receiving a bonus for a first purchase in a category. A promotion may set eligible members, products, dates, and caps. Vouchers give a member a reward or discount to use later. Badges and games can add engagement features. An Experience Cloud member portal can display points, tier, and vouchers.

blocks.heading: Partner programs
blocks.body: Loyalty programs may let members earn or redeem points with partners, such as earning hotel points through a car rental. Configure partner terms and track points issued or redeemed by each partner for settlement between companies. Partners commonly send transactions through APIs, after which the program’s journals and rules process them.

blocks.heading: Reporting and program value
blocks.body: Reports and Loyalty Analytics help teams review active membership, points earned and redeemed, tier changes, and promotion results. Points liability is the value of unspent points and an important finance measure. Combining loyalty, purchase, and marketing data—for example in Data Cloud—can support more relevant member offers.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Loyalty Management AP exam
scenarioTips.intro: Translate each program requirement into a currency, tier, process, or promotion setting that will make it happen.

blocks.heading: Set up the program first
blocks.body: Create the program and currencies, then configure tier groups and tiers. Attach member benefits to the appropriate tier.

blocks.heading: Trace earning and redemption
blocks.body: Activities become transaction journals. Program processes apply rules to award or remove points.

blocks.heading: Review the member lifecycle
blocks.body: Members enroll, earn points, move between tiers, and may become inactive. Tier reviews and expiry rules manage changes over time.

blocks.heading: Configure partner activity
blocks.body: Partners can submit transactions. Track each partner’s points earned and redeemed for settlement.

blocks.heading: Use loyalty reporting
blocks.body: Monitor points liability, redemption, tier movement, and promotion results.

sampleQuestions.question: Flight activity should count toward Gold status, but credit-card points should only be spendable. How should the program distinguish them?
options: Use one currency and remove tier status
sampleQuestions.explanation: Qualifying points count toward tiers. Non-qualifying points can be redeemed without changing status.
whyWrong: If all points qualify, credit-card activity could affect tier status.
If no points qualify, flight activity cannot advance a member’s tier.
This setup does not meet the requirement to use tiers.

sampleQuestions.question: A member buys a $120 jacket in a store. What record should be created before points are awarded?
options: A voucher for a future reward
A new tier for the member
sampleQuestions.explanation: Purchases are recorded as transaction journals, which program processes evaluate to award points.
whyWrong: A partner is another company in the loyalty program.
Vouchers represent rewards for later use.
Tiers are member status levels, not purchase records.

sampleQuestions.question: Gold members earn two points per dollar while other members earn one. Where should this rule be configured?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Program processes can apply accrual rules based on conditions such as tier.
whyWrong: A voucher is a reward, not an earning-rate rule.
Partner settings do not define member tier earning rates.
The address does not determine the point rate described.

sampleQuestions.question: The brand wants double points on purchases over a holiday weekend, capped at 500 bonus points per member. What should it configure?
options: Manual point adjustments for each member
A dated promotion with a member cap
sampleQuestions.explanation: A promotion can define dates, bonus earning, and a cap for each member.
whyWrong: A tier represents status, not a temporary offer.
Manual adjustments are difficult to manage at scale.
A new currency is unnecessary for a bonus.

sampleQuestions.question: Unspent points should expire after 24 months. What should be configured?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Expiry rules remove points after a defined period and help the business manage outstanding liability.
whyWrong: Partner agreements cover partner terms.
Tier groups organize status levels, not expiry.
Deleting members would remove their history.

sampleQuestions.question: A member asks why their points balance fell last month. Where can the agent review the changes?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The ledger records the member’s point changes, including earnings, redemptions, and expiry.
whyWrong: The partner list does not show a member’s transactions.
A tier definition explains status rules rather than balance history.
One promotion does not show every balance change.

sampleQuestions.question: Hotel members should earn points when they rent cars through a partner. What should the program add?
sampleQuestions.explanation: A program partner can send qualifying transactions under agreed partner terms.
whyWrong: Tiers define status, not participating companies.
Email is not a scalable transaction integration.
A separate program would split the member experience.

sampleQuestions.question: Finance asks for the value of points members have earned but not redeemed. What is this measure called?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Points liability measures the value of unspent points the business may need to honor.
whyWrong: Enrollment rate measures sign-ups.
Redemption rate measures how many points are used.
Tier movement measures status changes.

sampleQuestions.question: Gold members receive free delivery. Where should this benefit be configured?
options: As a benefit on the Gold tier
sampleQuestions.explanation: Benefits are attached to tiers so members receive them while they hold that status.
whyWrong: Currencies represent points.
Journals record activities and transactions.
Partners are other companies in the program.

sampleQuestions.question: A member reached Gold in March. When should the system check whether they retain the status?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Tier rules define review timing and the requirements for retaining status.
whyWrong: Tier status can be subject to review.
A support call does not trigger a tier review.
Logging in is unrelated to the tier schedule.

sampleQuestions.question: Members need to view points, tier, and vouchers online. What is a common solution?
options: Email a PDF statement each week
Ask members to call the contact center
Provide a member portal using Experience Cloud
sampleQuestions.explanation: Experience Cloud can host a portal where members can view loyalty information.
whyWrong: A PDF can become outdated between statements.
Phone support is slower and less convenient for routine viewing.
Chatter is not designed as a member portal.

sampleQuestions.question: After a promotion, marketing wants to know whether it increased spending. What should the team review?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Promotion reporting helps evaluate whether an offer changed member behavior.
whyWrong: Portal styling does not measure promotion performance.
Tier count does not show the promotion’s effect.
Expiry rules do not measure spending uplift.

sampleQuestions.question: A member returns a purchase that earned 120 points. What should the program do?
options: Move the member down a tier immediately
sampleQuestions.explanation: A return can be recorded as a journal so program rules can reverse the points associated with the purchase.
whyWrong: Deleting the member would remove unrelated history.
Tier changes follow tier rules rather than every return.
Keeping points for a returned purchase leaves the balance inaccurate.

sampleQuestions.question: The brand wants tailored offers based on loyalty, purchases, and web activity together. What helps unify these signals?
options: Keep each data set in a separate system
Bring the data together in Data Cloud
Ask every member to complete a survey
sampleQuestions.explanation: Data Cloud can unify information from different sources to support more relevant targeting.
whyWrong: Tier alone provides limited information.
Separate data makes it harder to personalize offers across behaviors.
Surveys do not capture all observed behavior.

sampleQuestions.question: A member earns a $10 discount to use on a later order. What should the program issue?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Vouchers represent rewards or discounts members can use later.
whyWrong: Partners are other participating companies.
Tier groups organize status levels.
A tier is a status level, not a redeemable discount.
